subject: Context & output sizing — pricing follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@peregrinelabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Context & output sizing — pricing follow-up and next steps

Jordan — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps for pricing: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary workloads: knowledge assistant (customer support triage) + daily batch vectorization for search indexing.
- Avg active users: 12k weekly; spike patterns with peak concurrency ~1.2k.
- Two traffic modes: interactive chat (low latency) and offline batch embedding runs.

Context / output profile you reported (please confirm):
- Avg prompt (including system + user): ~420 tokens
- Avg completion: ~180 tokens for chat; some long-form generation up to ~2k tokens for summaries (1-2% of calls)
- Embeddings: 512-d vectors, batch sizes ~50–100 per job; daily volume ~300k items
- Long-context needs: about 8% of calls require 32k context to stitch multi-document context; occasional legal/archival cases could benefit from 128k (negligible volume ~0.1%)

What we need from you to produce a tailored pricing snapshot:
1) Please confirm avg prompt/completion tokens by endpoint (chat vs summarization vs embeddings).
2) Expected monthly token volume ranges (low/expected/high). A useful bucket we use: 10M / 100M / 1B tokens.
3) Any hard budget bands (target $ / 1M tokens) or IO thresholds we should aim for.

Tentative next steps
- Rishi will produce a preliminary unit-econ sheet (per 1M tokens) and three provisioning profiles (low/typical/peak) for 8k/32k/128k context.
- We’ll send a small sample pricing workbook and a recommended rollout plan (start with chat + embeddings, gate 32k for the highest-value flows).

Attachments: I attached a blank pricing snapshot and a small CSV template where you can drop real token telemetry if available.

Thanks — aiming to get the snapshot back to you by EOD Wed PT.

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0194

From: Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@peregrinelabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Context & output sizing — pricing follow-up and next steps

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear write-up. Quick answers inline: 

> Avg prompt/completion tokens by endpoint
- Chat (support triage): prompt ~400 tokens / completion ~150 tokens (most are short confirmations).
- Summaries (daily legal summaries): prompt variable ~3k tokens / completion ~900–1,800 tokens (these are the long ones).
- Embeddings: prompt payload per item ~180 tokens (we include a short context slice).

> Monthly token volume buckets (low/expected/high)
- Low: ~25M tokens/month
- Expected: ~350M tokens/month
- High: ~1.2B tokens/month (includes seasonal spikes and new feature betas)

> Long-context needs
- 8k: majority of chat and small summaries — ~70%
- 32k: ~29% (stitching docs for case context)
- 128k: rare, about 0.5% — legal evidence pulls and long-form compliance exports

Budget target: we’re trying to land around $800–1,200 per 1M tokens for the initial phase (we are aware this varies by model and context length — want to know expected unit economics across the three context profiles).

I’m attaching anonymized daily sample telemetry (token counts per call) — should help you model real mix.

Jordan
Director of Product — AI
Peregrine Labs
jordan.peters@peregrinelabs.com

Attachment: peregrine_sample_profile.csv (text/csv)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Context & output sizing — pricing follow-up and next steps

Looping in a short pricing sketch based on Jordan’s buckets. High level assumptions (we’ll expand in workbook):
- Models: mix of optimized open variants (cost baseline) + fallback to higher-cost proprietary for 128k needs.
- Effective token cost drivers: context length (memory + KV-cache cost), completion avg length, batch efficiency (embeddings), and cache hit rate.

Prelim unit econ per 1M tokens (ballpark):
- 8k profile (typical chat mix) — $420 / 1M tokens
- 32k profile (doc stitching + longer completions) — $1,050 / 1M tokens
- 128k profile (rare long pulls) — $3,500 / 1M tokens (largely due to memory and model selection)

Using Jordan’s monthly expected mix (350M tokens) and reported distribution (~70% 8k, 29% 32k, 1% 128k):
- Weighted avg cost ~= (0.70*420 + 0.29*1050 + 0.01*3500) = ~$610 / 1M tokens

Notes / levers to lower cost:
- Prefix/KV caching on case context (target 15–25% hit rate) to materially reduce effective context tokens.
- Quantized model variants for high-volume chat flows.
- Reserve capacity (Dedicated) for predictable throughput could reduce unit cost by 12–20% depending on commit.

I’ll build a workbook with three scenarios (conservative/expected/aggressive) and include suggested commit tiers that hit Jordan’s target band of $800–1,200 per 1M tokens (as reference, expected shows ~ $610 — below target).

Rishi
Sr. Product Manager, Cost & Performance | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_pricing_snapshot.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@peregrinelabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Context & output sizing — pricing follow-up and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround and the sample telemetry. Attached is the workbook Rishi referenced with the three scenarios and a short playbook for rolling out 32k capability only to the high-value flows to control cost. Quick summary: 

What we recommend now
- Start: enable 8k optimized stack for chat + embeddings; use quantized open models for chat to get unit cost down.
- Phase 2: gate 32k to case-retrieval use-cases (29% of calls) and enable at canary traffic first; measure cache hit rate and completion quality.
- 128k: keep as on-demand fallback; show rate estimates and reserve only for rare legal exports.

Pricing highlights (see workbook tab "Summary")
- Expected weighted unit cost: ~$610 / 1M tokens (given current mix).
- If customer targets $800–1,200 / 1M, we can design a commit + reserved capacity plan that provides predictable latency and an approx 15% discount to hosted list pricing.

Next steps
- Jordan: confirm if we should draft a 3-month pilot contract with reserved baseline (we’ll mock commitments targeting 350M tokens/mo).
- Peregrine procurement: if you want, send a minimal SOW or PO and we’ll push an initial contract draft for review.

We’ll follow up with a short 30-minute session to walk through the workbook — propose Thu 18 Mar 2026 10:00 AM PT; tell us if that works.

Best —
Kimberly
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0194
